extracted.intended_audience: President and Council of Fort St. George; Company governors and colonial administrators (East India Company)
extracted.subtask_description: Official instructions and principles for settling the assignment of Carnatic revenues, arranging treaties for defence and military contributions, and distributing/handling the Nabob's private debts. Directed to the Company's local government (Madras/Fort St. George) for execution and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit demands on Rajah for past collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct to surcease any further demands from the Rajah in respect of parts of the government share of the crop collected by his people; accept the Rajah's deposit (one lac of pagodas) on account of the Nabob's claims until London’s sentiments are known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of lapse of time and uncertainty about exact balances and collections, do not compel the Rajah to pay supposed balances or render specific accounts; suspend further application of the deposit until any difficulty is explained and further orders received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rajah accountable only for admitted collections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Rajah ought to be answerable for no more than the amount he admits was collected by his people for the government share of the crop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proceedings do not sufficiently explain whether admitted sums include parts taken from assignees (e.g., Mr. Benfield), or what compensation has been made, withhold final disposition of deposits until clarified by the local government and reported for further orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend Rajah assist assignees in recovering debts
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should recommend the Rajah restore grain in possession of assignees and give reasonable assistance to assignees (e.g., Mr. Benfield) in recovering debts justly due from inhabitants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The recommendation was to leave manner and time to the Rajah, and not require him to be accountable for more than the government share; communications to the Rajah should encourage restoration and assistance rather than compulsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow and regulate repairs of Anicut and Cavery banks
rubrics_metrics.description: It is reasonable that the Rajah be permitted to repair the Anicut and banks of the Cavery as formerly practised; local government should establish effective regulations for keeping those banks in repair by reference to former usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to prior investigations and reports (1764, Bourchier survey, letters of 1765 and 1767). Establish regulations effectual to remove future cause of complaint and secure irrigation-dependent cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source repair materials from Trichinopoly under lease
rubrics_metrics.description: If expedient, apply to the Nabob to permit spots in Trichinopoly where the Rajah and his people may take sand and earth for repairs, and seek lease of such spots to the Company at reasonable annual rent for a term of years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials from Trichinopoly are preferable and cheaper; request the Nabob in the Company's name. Any lease should be limited in duration and intended to secure cultivation without impairing Nabob's rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditionality of Trichinopoly lease on punctual payments
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed lease of Trichinopoly material spots should remain in force only while the Rajah is punctual in payment of the annual peshcush to the Nabob and the reserved rent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie lease validity to punctual fulfillment of financial obligations to avoid long-term encroachment and to maintain balance between parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ Company-appointed engineers for works at Rajah's expense
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that skilful engineers, appointed by the Company, be employed at the Rajah's expense to conduct necessary repair works with strict attention to rights and interests of both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineers act under appointment of the Government of Madras; this removes probability of injury or dispute. If either party feels injured, immediate redress is to be obtained by application to Madras government rather than inter-party discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prevent diversion of Cavery water; seek Nabob’s assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: If attempts are or shall be made to divert Cavery water (e.g., into Coleroon by contracting current or planting long grass), represent the matter to the Nabob in the Company's name to prevent his people taking detrimental measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company expects Nabob, when properly represented, will prevent such actions, as he is materially interested in the prosperity of the Tanjore country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treaty principle: contracting parties jointly support military force
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct local government to impress upon the Nabob and Rajah the expediency of entering into treaty(s) with the Company obliging all contracting parties to contribute jointly to support the military force and garrisons in peace and war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treaties should be grounded on equity and include explicit obligations for contributions and support; use utmost endeavors to obtain their assent jointly or separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company to settle the military peace establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: The military peace establishment shall be forthwith settled and adjusted by the Company in pursuance of the authority and directions given by the late act of Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company has exclusive charge of defence; settlement must be punctual and accurate; arrangements should reflect statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure contributions by specifying districts/revenues with Company enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Nabob and Rajah must specify particular districts and revenues to secure due and regular payment of their contributions into the Company's treasury; Company has power in case of default to enter upon and possess such districts and let them to renters (confirmed by the sovereigns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enforcement power is coupled with Company assurances to support Nabob's and Rajah's dignity and exclusive civil administration; powers to enter on default are necessary to ensure punctuality.

rubrics_metrics.name: During war, aggregate revenues applied to common defence and not commercial use
rubrics_metrics.description: In case of hostility on the Coromandel coast, the whole revenues of respective territories shall be considered as one common stock for the common cause of defence; Company shall refrain during the war from applying revenues to commercial purposes (save ordinary civil charges) and apply them to the war.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nabob and Rajah shall similarly refrain from diverting revenues during war except for necessary civil support; this unity demonstrates combined defence and financial clarity to other powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain and protect civil establishment funds before war appropriation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertain the sum indispensably necessary for civil establishment and hold it sacred under every emergency, to be set apart previous to application of the rest of the revenues to war purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents misunderstanding and preserves peace by making finances clear and avoiding arbitrary appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Company administration and accounting for aggregate revenues
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole aggregate revenue shall be under Company application during war and as long after as necessary to discharge war-borne burdens; Company to produce regular accounts and faithfully apply funds to stipulated purposes, without depriving Nabob/Rajah of their authority to collect revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If revenues are diverted from stipulated purposes, the Company may take on collection; transparency and regular accounts are required to maintain trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit Nabob/Rajah troops; Company to furnish military aid when required
rubrics_metrics.description: Nabob shall agree not to maintain more troops than necessary (specified number in treaty) for dignity and durbar splendor; if additional military aid is needed for revenue security/collection, the Company must furnish such aid. Rajah of Tanjore shall have similar engagements and entitlements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces unnecessary expense and harmonizes military responsibilities among contracting parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and, if possible, confirm existing renters' leases
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply to the Nabob for consent that renters, whose leases were granted under Lord Macartney’s agreement, be permitted to hold leases to the end of the stipulated term; if Nabob objects, do not insist as essential but indemnify renters for reasonable loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Company relies on Nabob’s liberality but, failing consent, local government must ensure reasonable indemnification to renters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect natives who faithfully administered collections
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that natives who were put in authority over collections by assignment and who proved faithful shall not suffer inconvenience on account of their fidelity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Honor the service of local officials and provide protection/indemnity where due to their faithful performance under the assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coercive measures (e.g., issuing Torana Chits) require absolute necessity and prior conciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The issuance of Torana Chits in Lord Macartney’s name can only be justified on the ground of absolute necessity; greater use should have been made of address, civility, and conciliation beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precautions and proof of necessity should precede coercive acts; omission is blameworthy where diplomacy might have avoided offence to Nabob’s authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt official communication of peace to native sovereigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Official communication of the peace should be made promptly to the Nabob; failure to do so (e.g., delay near a month) is reprehensible and a mark of disrespect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On all occasions pay the highest attention to the Nabob and his family to avoid impressions of disrespect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate opinions with prudence and discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Opinions and speculations communicated to the Board (e.g., about native powers) should be conveyed with prudence, discretion, secrecy, and in terms as little offensive as possible to the powers they concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While collection and communication of intelligence is applauded, avoid terms or expressions that might be offensive if they fall into hands of concerned native powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classify and treat Nabob's private debts according to origin and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish debts consolidated in 1767 (treated as constituted by original bonds at 10% interest), the Cavalry Loan (1777) at 12%, and the consolidated debt of 1777 with adjusted interest (12% to Nov 1781 then 6% thereafter); only recognize or protect debts consistent with justice and legislative provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The loan of 1767 is treated as valid at 10% interest and protected; the 1777 consolidated debt is on less favourable footing but admitted to participation subject to complaints and examination. No sanction is given to debts without express authority of Court of Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow complaints on 1777 debts and transmit evidence for decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the 1777 debts are admitted to participation, receive complaints by the Nabob or other interested parties alleging injustice, attentively examine grounds and transmit evidence to the Directors for final decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local government must forward complaints and evidence; admissions to protection are provisional and subject to further investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution rules for the twelve lacs of pagodas fund
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a precise priority distribution: (1) growing interest on Cavalry Loan at 12%; (2) growing interest on debt of 1777 at 6%; remainder equally divided — one half to Company's debt, the other half to pay growing interest at 10% and principal of debt of 1767; successive stages specified for discharge and reallocation once loans are paid off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed stepwise allocation continues until the debt of 1767 is discharged, then reallocates amounts (e.g., when Cavalry Loan discharged, seven lacs to Company's debt and five lacs to 1777 loan). If Tanjore peshcush arrears are applied, they should reduce Company’s debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require creditor acquiescence and exclude refractory creditors
rubrics_metrics.description: Creditors under Company protection must express acquiescence in the distribution arrangements; any creditor refusing acquiescence is excluded from fund distribution and prohibited from separate measures to recover debt, and refractory creditors shall be dismissed from service and sent home to England.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition aims to relieve the Nabob from individual creditor importunities and secure finality; local government to enforce exclusion and dismissal where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: No protection for newly alleged debts until investigation and instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: If further debts have been contracted recently (surmised), and if due to British subjects, forbid any countenance or protection to be given to them until the debt is fully investigated, nature reported home, and special instructions received from Directors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protective measures limited to debts that have been properly reported and investigated; avoid recognizing or enabling unexamined claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict prohibition on Company servants engaging in money transactions with country powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeat prohibition that no servant of the Company, or person under its protection, shall have any loan or money transaction with country powers without knowledge and express permission of the respective governments; offenders to be sent home and denied protection for recovery of such loans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an absolute prohibition (repeated in strongest terms); breaches are treated as disobedience of orders and will incur highest displeasure and punitive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit undue intercourse between British subjects and Nabob’s family
rubrics_metrics.description: Strong prohibition against intercourse between British subjects and the Nabob and his family to prevent intrigues that have been detrimental to the Nabob and advantageous to individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct that any person offending against this prohibition, whether in Company service or under protection, be forthwith sent to England.
